object_description: compact western ensemble with a dominant school volume and sunken gymnasium
design_condition: The compact buildings are concentrated on the west to place the football field farther west and integrate the lawn into the terrain, while stairs, squares and planted edges organize connections to the surrounding district.

positive.statement: The compact western disposition optimizes the placement of the football field in relation to the topography.
The new school building establishes a clear volumetric focus and strengthens the connection to the district.
The topographical conditions generate differentiated outdoor spaces and organize access to the different user groups.
The address square provides an arrival point that can also accommodate events.
The compact organization supports the educational concept of the small school within the larger school.
The separate gymnasium and auditorium arrangement provides independence for larger events, clubs and neighbourhood use.
The facade design makes a high-quality impression and conveys a certain openness.

negative.statement: The compact urban-planning strategy leaves the surrounding open spaces limited and lacking spatial and atmospheric power.
The prominent outside-stair transitions are neither adequate nor practical for people with disabilities.
The access areas are generously sized but uninspiring, functioning more as corridors than lounges.
The childcare rooms are only vertically connected through the general staircase, restricting flexibility of use.
The potential for networking public uses with the outdoor space and district is not exploited.
The gymnasium entrance is difficult to read because of its lateral placement beneath the massive school volume and the adjacent outside staircase.
The overall appearance is not considered adequate for a primary school in relation to the impressive size of the new building.
